ai.title: Rework evalbuff: commit learning, parallel agents, trace compression
ai.summary: Evalbuff restructured around two modes: Commit Learning (default) walks git history oldest-first, generating vague prompts from diffs and running N parallel agents (default 5) against parent commits, with state saved per-commit for resume; Prompt Mode runs a single prompt without git history. New `commit-task-generator.ts` extracts commit info, filters merge/initial commits, and caps diffs at 200k chars. `trace-compressor.ts` added to compress agent traces before feeding them to the doc-writer agent, reducing token usage. `cli-runner.ts` now spawns detached process groups and kills the entire tree on timeout via `process.kill(-pid, 'SIGKILL')`, preventing orphaned child processes.

eli5.text: Evalbuff, the system that watches a coding assistant struggle with real tasks and then writes documentation to help it do better next time, has been rebuilt to work smarter. It now walks through your project's git history oldest-first, and instead of trying one task at a time, it can run several attempts in parallel against each commit, saving its progress so it can pick up where it left off if interrupted. It also squeezes down the verbose logs those attempts produce before analyzing them, so the doc-writing step uses less computing power. On top of that, when an attempt times out, the system now properly cleans up the whole tree of helper processes it spawned, preventing leftover zombie tasks. Everything described here is active as of March 27, 2026.

ai.title: Remove wait-for command from tmux CLI agent
ai.summary: The tmux CLI agent helper script no longer supports the `wait-for` command. The implementation in `agents/tmux-cli.ts` has been removed, along with all references in usage strings, system prompts, and documentation. Users and agents must now rely exclusively on `wait-idle` to stabilize output before sending further input.

eli5.text: If you use an automated assistant that runs a program inside a terminal window and then types into it, that assistant can no longer tell the program to 'pause until a specific line of text shows up', a feature called 'wait-for' has been removed. The assistant must now only use 'wait-idle', which pauses until the output stops changing for a few seconds. If you write or rely on instructions that say to wait for exact phrases to appear, those instructions will no longer work; you should switch them to wait for the screen to go quiet instead. This change is already live.
